spec.name: rot_mixed_keyed_chain_v2
spec.limitations: Still byte-local: each output byte depends only on the matching input byte, so repeated plaintext bytes stay repeated and no message-level structure is hidden. The key is a single byte, so a 256-key exhaustive search recovers it trivially from any known or guessed plaintext pair, and the key enters at only two points; rotations and modular carries also make the map non-affine over Z_256, so the legitimate inverse has no simple algebraic shortcut either. Length and ordering are unauthenticated.
spec.math: Each primitive is a bijection of Z_256: add c: x -> (x+c) mod 256; xor n: x -> x XOR n; xor_key: x -> x XOR k; add_key: x -> (x+k) mod 256; rol r: x -> ((x<<r) OR (x>>(8-r))) mod 256 with rotation amount r mod 8. Composing bijections gives a bijection, hence exact invertibility. The forward map is: x -> rol4( xor200( add_k( rol2( add9( xor_key( rol5( add112(x) ))))))), and its inverse applies, in reverse order: rol 4 again (since 8-4=4), xor 200, sub_key (add (256-k)), rol 6, sub 9, xor_key, rol 3, sub 112.
spec.assumptions: Secret key byte k is fixed per challenge, uniform over 0..255, and substituted by the engine for both *_key placeholders, whose operands (0) are ignored; public constants 112, 9, 200 and the rotation amounts are known to the receiver; the inverse is run with the same k in reverse step order.
